A1.justification: Both PDFs describe E(3)-Pose and contain readable main text, equations, figures, tables, and appendices. Corresponding material can be matched despite substantial reformatting and relocation.

before.justification: v5 reports original fetal MRI experiments, baseline comparisons, ablations, sensitivity analyses, and quantitative slice-prescription simulations.

after.justification: v6 retains these original empirical results and adds training-convergence results in Appendix J, Fig. 14.

M1.justification: The stated loss changes from a fixed pseudovector coefficient and shared vector weight beta in v5 Eq. (7) to separate beta_x, beta_y, and beta_z weights in v6 Eq. (6). This generalizes the specified objective; the architecture and inference procedure remain unchanged. Actual weight changes or retraining are not established.

E1.justification: The four benchmark datasets and simulated test scenarios are unchanged. Appendix A changes from describing ongoing evaluation of full in-utero slice prescription to reporting that it has been performed. Without additional cohort or evaluation details, it is unclear whether this represents expanded clinical test coverage or a status update on the previously described work.

E2.justification: The evaluated baselines remain FireANTs, EquiTrack, Fetal-Align, 3DPose-Net, 6DRep, and RbR, with the same documented adaptations. The simulation comparator remains motion-blind prescription. The new convergence analysis uses existing ablation variants.

E3.justification: The new convergence analysis evaluates rotation error over the first 1000 training epochs on in-distribution data and Navigators under both training datasets. Existing splits, preprocessing, metrics, and full training budgets are unchanged; the curves do not establish a reduced training budget.

E4.justification: v6 Appendix J adds an analysis of convergence with and without reflection symmetry and rotation equivariance. The intensity and spatial sensitivity studies already existed in v5 Appendix J; their relocation to Section 5.6 and Fig. 4 is not a new robustness experiment.

E5.justification: v6 removes subject-level permutation-test significance reporting from Tables 4–8 while retaining their 95% confidence intervals. Dataset-level Wilcoxon and hierarchical permutation tests remain, with an added explanation of temporal and subject correlations. Neither version establishes additional repeated runs or seeds.

E6.justification: All numerical mean and dispersion entries in Tables 1–9 are retained. v6 adds convergence curves reporting faster convergence and updates the qualitative in-utero implementation status. Selected Navigators significance markers disappear, including the Research-Fetal-trained geodesic-loss rotation result in Table 2 and both comparator results in Table 3.

T1.justification: Appendix D corrects the reversed monotonicity descriptions of the loss terms. Appendix J adds explicit sign-flip derivations and a geodesic-loss counterexample beyond v5's brief argument. Most reflection and rotational-symmetry derivations already existed; theorem labels alone are presentational. The new SVD counterexample contains notation and numerical inaccuracies.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same central contributions: equivariant, reflection-aware pose estimation, robust generalization to clinical fetal MRI, and potential support for adaptive slice prescription.

C2.justification: v6 adds interpretations connecting baseline rankings to continuous rotation representations and convergence curves to architectural inductive biases. Appendix A explicitly separates technical development from future diagnostic evaluation. The principal limitations concerning pathology, uncertainty, and the small, single-institution Navigators cohort remain.

D1.justification: The architecture specifications, augmentation distributions, optimizers, training budgets, hardware, scanner parameters, annotation procedures, and code/data access information are retained. The deployment-status update does not document a different implementation procedure or newly available resource.

R1.justification: v6 adds Baxter's A Model of Inductive Bias Learning to support the convergence interpretation. Appendix A also clarifies the relationship to the authors' clinical implementation abstract. Most other reference changes are formatting, reordering, or metadata updates.

P1.justification: There is broad copyediting but limited narrative restructuring: sensitivity analysis moves into the main text, references move after the appendices, and mathematical explanations adopt lemma/theorem formatting. Author ordering and affiliation text also change. The principal section sequence and much of the prose remain recognizable.

P2.justification: The document switches from two-column to single-column layout and extensively reformats tables and figures. v5 Figs. 4, 14, and 15 become the composite v6 Fig. 4; convergence curves are added, simulation boxplots become violin plots, and qualitative comparison rows are reordered. These are substantial visual changes beyond pagination.

improvement.justification: The convergence curves provide useful evidence about the architectural choices, Appendix D corrects the loss explanation, and the clinical scope is more clearly qualified. These yield a limited overall gain while the benchmark results remain unchanged. The expanded mathematics still needs correction: Appendix J omits the determinant in its SVD correction and reports approximately pi/6 for a projection whose stated inputs yield pi/8. These localized defects limit the improvement.
